message.reasoning:
I'm figuring out tempo and bar count to fit a two-minute track cleanly — settling on 100 BPM for 50 bars of 4/4, landing exactly at 120 seconds.

I'm now thinking through timing resolution using ticks per beat, and defining each drum hit deterministically with fixed seed-based humanization instead of pure randomness — laying the snare slightly late and hi-hats slightly early for feel. I need to enforce limb constraints so no more than one event per limb happens at the same tick, accounting for hands, feet, and flams, then sketching the intro bars with a sparse toms-based motif.

Now I'm mapping out the full 60-bar arc: a groove section with swung hi-hats and ghost notes, a varied restatement of the motif with rising density, a Latin percussion breakout using congas and cowbell, a build back into the full kit, a quiet breakdown with cross-stick, and building toward a climactic double-kick section.

Then I'm working out the swing math—computing tick offsets for delayed odd 16ths and pushed hi-hats at 120 BPM with a 0.58 swing ratio—before starting to sketch out the code framework for generating this drum pattern.

Writing helper functions...

I'm working out the swing curve math so 32nd notes stay proportionally placed, then setting swing ratios per section—around 0.58 generally, slightly tighter at 0.55 for the climax to add drive. I'm also assigning feel offsets per instrument, laying the snare back a bit and pushing the hats/ride forward, plus adding tiny randomized micro-timing variation for humanization.

Now I'm mapping out velocity dynamics—ghost notes around 25-40, normal hits 70-85, accents 110-127—scaled by a per-bar intensity function that builds crescendos, and cross-referencing the GM drum voice numbers to assign the right instrument for each hit.

I want the hi-hat choke behavior (open then closed/pedal) to rely on the synth's exclusive class handling rather than manual note-offs. Now I'm sketching Motif A, the signature hook pattern, placing accented 16th-note hits at specific steps within the bar to give it a distinctive groove.

I'm defining the motif's rhythm as a clave-inspired pattern with onsets at steps 0, 3, 6, 10, and 12, then pairing each onset with a contour level and accent flag so I can later map pitch levels onto actual drum voices in the kit.

Now I'm thinking through variation techniques—displacement, augmentation, diminishing, gap-filling with ghost notes, and contour inversion—plus a contrasting Motif B built on a 3-over-4 sticking pattern for use in the build section, and I'm working out how to alternate hands across the limbs when assigning each motif note.

Setting sticking rules with collision checks...

Defining GM percussion note constants...

I'm assigning timing offsets by drum type: snares hit slightly late, cymbals slightly early, ghost notes even lazier, giving the groove a human feel. I'm starting a Solo class to structure improvisational patterns.

Writing swing timing logic...

For the dynamic curve, I'm defining a piecewise velocity envelope using breakpoints across the song's bars, interpolating linearly between them to shape intensity, then multiplying base velocities by this level and clamping to valid MIDI range.

Now I'm planning velocity ranges (ghost 38, normal 85, accent 120) and sketching out section 1, the intro over bars 0-3: motif A stated on toms with sparse kick, hi-hat pulsing quarter notes for time-keeping, and a bar 1 answer that thins out to ghost snare hits before the motif returns with variation in bar 2.

For section 2, the groove starting at bar 4, I'm working out swung 8th-note hi-hat patterns with quarter-note accents and occasional open hi-hat on the last 8th, figuring out how the foot pedal needs to close it before the next downbeat.

I'm layering ghost notes on the snare backbeat while keeping the kick pattern tied to motif A's rhythm, syncing the kick's accented hits with the snare backbeats where they naturally overlap.

For structure, I'm planning fills at bars 7 and 11 that surface the motif on toms, adding crash accents on bars 4 and 8, then developing the motif further across bars 12-19 with ghost-note variations and steady foot patterns before displacing the motif rhythmically in later bars.

I'm working through diminution (compressing the motif into half-bar repetitions) and building density with doubles and ruffs into a crescendo roll leading into bar 20, then reindexing so the Latin section falls at bars 20-27 with a lighter swing feel, tumbao-style kick pattern, and cowbell or cascara on top.

Since there's no shell sample in GM, I'm mapping the timbale cascara onto cowbell/agogo instead, and working out a conga tumbao with muted heel-toe strokes, a slap accent on beat 2, and open tones landing on beat 4 and the "and" of 4.

I'm also thinking about freeing up a foot for the clave -- using the left foot on a cowbell/woodblock pedal to play the son clave 3-2 pattern while the hands handle the conga tumbao.

Then I'm layering the kick on tumbao bass anticipations (steps 6 and 12), and planning a bongo/timbale/conga motif for the following bars using a contour map across the drum voices with ghost conga notes filling in.

Bar 27 gets a timbale "abanico" roll—rimshot buildup with 32nd-note crescendo—leading into the build section starting bar 28, where I'm shifting the swing feel and introducing a three-note linear cell (ride bell, ghost snare, kick) repeated as polyrhythmic groups of three against the underlying four, rising in dynamics through bars 28-29.

Bars 30-31 move that same three-note cell onto the toms, bars 32-33 bring back the original motif with full sixteenth-note density and crash accents, and bars 34-35 escalate into a snare/tom roll build with driving kick pattern, crescendoing toward a possible dramatic silence or break right before the next section.

Then I'm sketching the breakdown at bars 36-43: pianissimo dynamics, swing set to 0.6, and a jazz-style ride pattern with a swung skip note leading into beats 2 and 4, working out how a sixteenth-note swing grid can approximate that classic "ding-ding-a-ding" feel.

For the buildup and climax I'm layering in ride bell accents, hi-hat pedal on 4 and 12, side stick playing motif A quietly with ghost snares and feathered kicks, then having the motif call-and-response between side stick and toms crescendo into a crash-ride transition. Bars 44-55 kick off the climax with swing tightened to 0.55 and double bass sixteenths alternating between two kick voices under an accented restatement of motif A.

I'm accenting motif A with crash/china plus snare hits together, filling unaccented spaces with descending toms, then contrasting with a half-time shuffle groove at bars 48-49 using china eighths and a backbeat snare, before bars 50-51 bring a tom-melody solo with the motif diminished into sixteenth-note flams across the toms.

For the peak at bars 52-55, I'm laying down 32nd-note single-stroke tom runs descending in one-beat cells with crash accents landing on each downbeat alongside kick, then hitting a stop-time break at bar 55 where the full kit slams motif A in unison with silence in between for maximum contrast. The final section (bars 56-59) recalls the intro softly on toms, gradually building volume and kick support as it winds toward the ending.

For the closeout I'm building a crescendo snare roll from pianissimo to fortissimo through bar 59, then landing on a massive final hit combining both crashes and kick right on the bar 59 downbeat with a long ring-out, skipping any extra cymbal flourish like a vibraslap or triangle as too cheesy. Timing-wise I'm aiming for the final hit around 118 seconds with the ring extending to 120, ending the whole track cleanly at bar 60. Now I'm setting up motif A as a data structure encoding each note's step position, contour, and accent level.

Adding accent velocity mapping and displacement logic...

I'll define a helper that assigns hands by step index parity, but I need to check whether this breaks down in grooves where ghost snare notes and hi-hat hits share the same hand across syncopated 16th positions, especially with swing timing tightening the gap between consecutive same-hand hits.

I'm setting a minimum interval threshold per limb (around 55 ticks) to catch cases where swung 32nd notes compress too close together for one hand to physically play, while picking ghost note placements that avoid sitting right next to the backbeat.

I'll alternate hands for fast 32nd-note runs so each hand only needs to hit 16th-note speed, then set validation to drop notes within 45 ticks of a kept note (keeping whichever has higher velocity), and add short 40-tick note durations so retriggered notes don't cut off their own note-offs.

Now I'm sorting all events into absolute tick positions, ordering note-offs before note-ons at the same tick for determinism, and adding the necessary meta events like tempo, time signature, and track name. I also need to clamp any negative-tick swing offsets to zero so the first hit doesn't fall before the start of the bar.

Writing timing offset logic...

Still writing intro bars...

Filling out bar 3 with a crescendo fill and setting up bar 4 with a crash entrance, then writing a helper function to build the groove pattern for bars 4-11 with swing timing.

I'm working out safe ghost-note placements that avoid overlapping with the snare backbeat or hi-hat limb timing, settling on a few candidate patterns like [7,9,15] and [2,7,10,15] that keep enough gap between hits for the same hand.

Now I'm sketching kick patterns and mapping out the full bar structure from 4 through 11 — assigning ghost/kick combos per bar, adding a crash on bars 4, 8, and building a fill in bar 7 using the first three notes of the motif shifted to start at step 8, then planning a denser filled-motif fill across bar 11.

For section 3 (bars 12-19), I'm setting up a softer "four on the floor" kick feel with feathering, then working out how to layer a crash into bar 12 without clashing with the motif's tom hit at step 0 — considering adding a `first_crash` option to the motif function to handle that overlap cleanly.

Bars 12-13 map the motif onto snare/tom orchestration with ghost fills on odd steps, lighter in bar 12 and full with a pickup in bar 13. Bars 14-15 use displaced motif variations shifted forward, and I'm working through how displaced steps that overflow past 16 should wrap into the following bar.

For bar 14 the motif shifts by 2 steps and bar 15 by 4, but shift-by-4 collides with the crash at the start of bar 16, so I'm switching to a shift of 3 instead to avoid clashing hand assignments, checking left/right parity for each hit and layering in ghost notes and kick support under the accents. Bars 16-17 apply diminution, halving the motif's step spacing so it repeats twice as fast within each bar.

For that halved grid I'm mapping hand parity onto 32nd-note indices, orchestrating the toms high-to-low then low-to-high across the two bars, with kicks reinforcing accents and a steady quarter-note hi-hat pedal underneath. Bar 18 inverts the motif's contour across the toms, pairing crash-plus-kick on accented hits with left-hand tom ghosts elsewhere, and bar 19 builds a crescendoing 32nd snare roll through the first three beats before everything cuts to a unified crash-and-kick hit, followed by a brief silence that sets up a softer entrance into the Latin section.

Now I'm defining the Latin section (bars 20-27) with a swung feel: kick anticipating the tumbao on the "2&" and "4," clave rhythm split across the bars in a 3-2 pattern, and a conga tumbao pattern alternating muted heel/toe ghosts with open slaps and open tones to fill out the groove.

I'm also weaving in bongo martillo embellishments in a couple of bars and sketching a motif that shifts across a mapped percussion set (timbale, bongo, conga highs/lows), with ghost conga fills bridging the gaps and a cowbell cascara pattern starting to take shape.

Now I'm working out the RH cowbell mambo bell pattern with accented quarters and offbeats, while the LH plays fragments of the motif on timbales or bongo, trying to keep the two hands' rhythms complementary without overlapping steps.

I'm settling on having LH cover the full motif on timbales/congas while RH holds the bell pattern for bar 25, then displacing that motif by two steps with muted congas in bar 26, and sketching an abanico fill to open bar 27.

Now I'm mapping out the build section starting at bar 28, shifting swing to 0.58 and laying a continuous linear 3-cell pattern across bars 28-29 that alternates hands and foot hits, with the hi-hat marking each group's start.

For the ride sections I'll switch to R on ride with LF chick on beats 4 and 12 to avoid clashing with the hi-hat. Bars 30-31 use a 3-cell grouping alternating tom hits on R with snare ghosts on L and kick on RF, building dynamic intensity, then bars 32-33 bring back motif A with crash accents layered on top of the kick.

For the fill variation, I'm having L handle the unaccented motif notes plus fills while R stays reserved for crash hits on the accents, keeping the accent parity (steps 0, 6, 12) mapped to crash+kick hits. The remaining steps get filled with descending tom/snare hits at medium velocity to keep the texture dense, with the pedal holding quarter-note time underneath, and bar 34 turns the motif into a snare roll with matching accents.

For bar 35 I'm considering a descending 32nd-note tom run building crescendo through step 11, then a china+kick hit on step 12 followed by silence or a soft ride into the breakdown, similar to the earlier stop-time device in bar 19 but distinct enough to avoid repetition.

Moving into the breakdown section (bars 36-43), I'm setting a lazier swing feel with ride quarters at moderate velocity, pedal on beats 2 and 4, feathered kick hits, and starting the left hand with the side-stick motif from bar 36.

Then I'm developing that motif through the breakdown: bar 37 answers with ghost snare hits, bar 38 displaces the motif by two steps, bar 39 has toms echo the contour, bars 40-41 stretch the motif into an augmented clave-like pattern across two bars, and bar 42 sets up a call-and-response between a diminished side-stick motif and a tom answer.

For the climax section (bars 44-55, swing 0.55), I'm building double-bass 16th feet patterns split between right and left foot, with hands playing an accented motif using crash and snare hits on strong beats and toms filling the gaps, working out the exact 8th-note distribution between hands.

For bars 48-49 I'm easing into half-time with double bass dropping out, kick on the motif rhythm, china crashing on quarters, and snare working accents against ghost notes for contrast against the busier sections. Then bars 50-51 pick back up with the diminished motif repeating.

For 50-51 I'm adding flams to the tom accents, with the grace note struck by the opposite hand slightly ahead of the main hit, plus alternating kick and pedal patterns underneath. Bars 52-54 build to the peak with descending 32nd-note single strokes across the toms alternating hands, crash and kick landing together on the first hit of each beat.

Bar 53 varies this with ascending groupings on beats 2 and 4, and bar 54 fills in the motif with crash accents at max density, echoing the earlier accent pattern from bar 32. Bar 55 starts a stop-time tutti section where each onset stacks crash, kick, and snare together.

Then I'm easing off — bars 56-59 pull back to a quiet recall, with soft toms and gentle feet pedaling reintroducing the intro motif at low dynamic before building through pickups, a crescendo snare roll, and flam accents into a final crash hit at bar 59.

I'm mapping out the overall dynamic envelope across the whole piece as breakpoints tied to bar position, interpolating linearly between them, with the crescendo roll in bar 58 handled as its own separate ramp, then translating dynamic levels into actual velocity values with a bit of random jitter for humanization.

I'm reconsidering the ghost note velocities since a straight scaling makes them too quiet to register in GM synths, so I'm applying a gentler curve for low-level hits while keeping normal scaling for louder ones. I'm also double-checking limb assignments to make sure no more than two hands and two feet strike simultaneously, and confirming the left foot cleanly handles hi-hat pedal, claves, and kick duties without overlap conflicts, including checking the hi-hat pedal close timing against nearby hits.

Now I'm sketching the motif function that iterates through a sequence of steps, assigning limbs and velocities based on accent level, then working out a helper to determine which hand plays a given step based on whether it falls on a 16th or 32nd subdivision.

Setting up file and imports...

Defining more drum mappings...

Now I'm defining the hit function, which computes timing with humanization (feel adjustment plus gaussian jitter) and velocity scaling based on level and a random tweak, then appends the event tuple.

I'm writing the feel function to add timing offsets per instrument type - snare/clap hits land slightly late, hi-hats/rides slightly early, toms a bit late, kicks/crashes on time - with extra lag for quiet hits, giving the groove a human push-pull feel.

Now I'm writing a cleanup function that sorts events and merges duplicates hitting the same lane within a tight time window, keeping the louder of two near-simultaneous hits and discarding the weaker one.

Grace notes for flams should fall well outside that merge window relative to the other hand's prior note, so timing looks safe. Now I'm setting up the MIDI file structure—single track, type 0, 480 ticks per beat—and adding the track name, tempo, and time signature meta messages before writing the actual drum events.

Building note-on/off pairs from the event list...

I calculate the end-of-track tick at bar 60 and confirm it's beyond the last message before converting to delta times. Now I'm writing the intro section function, setting up hi-hats, the motif on toms, kick pattern, and ghost snare hits with a ride bell accent.

Continuing the drum pattern logic...

Defining groove patterns...

Still writing the fill helper...

For the dev section, I'm sketching a plan to shift swing, add hi-hat pedal accents in bars 12-18, then build bar 12 with a crash-kick hit on beat one, layering the motif on the kit, and adding ghost notes on odd steps.

Still writing drum arrangement logic...

For bar 16, using accents at 3,9,15 for the kick placement, and considering dropping the crash idea since layering it with the tom hit felt risky given the velocity ordering — simplifying to just kick on accent steps instead.

Working through the hand placements for right and left across the sixteen-step bar with swing timing, checking each interval stays above the minimum tick threshold. One placement (step 1.5 left hand) comes out borderline at 50 ticks with swing applied, so I'm avoiding it and moving ghost notes to steps 7 and 15 instead where spacing is safer.

Now I'm sketching bars 17 through 19: bar 17 splits the motif into two halves using toms then kit sounds, bar 18 inverts the motif with crash accents on the strong beats and a dense spread of tom hits on the left-hand odd steps, and bar 19 closes with a roll into a stop.

I'm writing a helper function to handle "crash-accent" hits, where accented steps trigger a crash plus kick on one hand and a unison snare on the opposite hand, while unaccented steps just play the mapped sound at the accent velocity. I need to watch out for collisions when the unison snare lands on a step where the other hand already has a fill note nearby.

I'm sketching a latin rhythm function with swing timing, alternating clave patterns between bars, and kick placement on specific 16th-note steps.

Now I'm working out the tumbao pattern for congas — left hand playing muted heel-toe eighth notes while the right hand adds slaps and open tones at specific steps, with variant bars introducing extra bongo hits.

For bars 24-27 I'm sketching the fill sequence: muted congas repeating the motif, a cowbell pattern with mambo-style accents on the right hand paired with the left hand motif, then a shifted variant with an added timbale hit, ending with a diminishing motif that speeds into thirty-second notes.

Writing build function...

Bar 32 does a tom fill descending from hi to floor toms based on position, with occasional kicks on accents. Bar 33 inverts the motif with a pickup fill and considers a china crash. Bar 34 switches to sixteenth-note snare with accents on motif onsets at higher velocity and kicks on the off-eighths.

Bar 35 builds a descending thirty-second note tom run across the beat, crescendoing before a big hit combining china, kick, and snare together, then cutting to silence. I'm now planning the breakdown section for bars 36-43 with a slower swing feel, using ride patterns, light hi-hat chick accents, and soft feathered kick hits, starting with bar 36 playing the main motif on sticks forced to the left hand.

I'm working through ghost snare placements, stick accents, and shifted/augmented versions of the motif across bars 37-42, alternating between soft tom answers, scaled-up rhythmic patterns that span across bar boundaries, and added kick accents, building toward a diminished pattern that splits sticks and toms across the bar's two halves.

Now I'm mapping bars 43-44: right hand ride pattern until step 12, left-hand ghost notes on odd steps crescendoing from 30 to 70, then a four-way tom fill across both hands in the last four steps with a kick on 14, plus hi-hat chick pattern through the first half. The dynamics ramp from 0.62 to 0.88 across bars 42-44, setting up the climax section starting at bar 44 with swing reset to zero.

For bars 44-48, I'm alternating kick hits on even steps (with extra accent on quarter-note downbeats) and a second kick voice on left foot for odd steps, layering the tom motif in unison across both hands with accented kicks. I'm adding china cymbal and snare accents to fill out the groove, then shifting the tom motif for bar 45 with accented hits on the floor tom for the offbeat pattern.

For bar 47, since accent steps land on left-hand strikes, I'm swapping in a second crash cymbal specifically for left-hand accents so the pattern stays balanced. Moving into bars 48-49, I'm shifting to a half-time feel with china cymbal eighth notes accented at the start and midpoint, paired with snare hits and ghost notes on the left hand.

For the kick pattern in these half-time bars, I'm working out placements at steps like 0,3,6,10 for one bar and 0,6,10,12,14 for the next, with foot-pedal hi-hat closures layered in, ending bar 49 with a small tom fill splitting hands between hi and mid toms.

For bars 50-51, I'm building a diminished version of the original motif played twice through the four-tom sequence, normal then inverted, and adding grace notes on neighboring toms just before accented hits to create a flam effect.

I'm checking timing so grace notes don't collide with the previous hand's hit, then planning bars 52-53 as descending 32nd-note runs across the beat with crash and kick accents, switching to china cymbal on certain beats, before moving into bar 54 with the motif plus a pickup phrase and double bass kicks across the toms.

For bar 55 I'm designing a stop-time tutti section where accented hits trigger all four limbs at once (crash, snare, and both kicks), while other notes use tom hits with the right-hand kick, leaving a brief silent gap before a quiet recall. Then I start sketching the ending bars 56-57 with a softer swing feel, alternating motif phrases across the toms with kick placement tied to the accent pattern.

Now I'm working out bar 58 as a build-up: a fast 32nd-note snare roll with velocity ramping upward through the bar, growing quarter-note kicks, and offbeat hi-hat pedal chicks, before shifting the last few steps to descending tom hits for a dramatic close into beat 14-15 with accented floor tom hits.

Then bar 59 hits with a full crash on both hands plus double kick at max velocity to mark the climax. I'm checking the overall timing math — total track length lands around 118-120 seconds, which works with the tail ring-out. I'm also confirming the swing settings vary deliberately across sections (Latin, breakdown, climax) for distinct feels, and the breakdown ride pattern has a slight rushed feel that I'm happy with.

Now I'm defining the helper functions carefully: a hand-alternation function based on step position and resolution, then the play() function that determines resolution automatically from the sequence, assigns hands, applies velocity accents, and optionally layers a kick under accented hits. I'm double-checking resolution detection works correctly for mixed sequences with both integer and half-step timings, and confirming ghost-note velocity thresholds use the base velocity before dynamics scaling. Writing the fill-pattern function next...

Checking the dynamic level scaling at bar 44 brings the base velocity down to 107. I'm defining a descending tom fill helper that cycles through toms based on position, and confirming the conga mute setup for Latin patterns works as a high-velocity mute hit.

I'm considering adding tone color for the whole percussion set — maybe a hi-hat-mounted tambourine substituting for the pedal hi-hat during the breakdown at bars 40-43, since only one note fits per limb at a time. I'm also thinking about tossing in a splash cymbal somewhere around bar 16 for extra texture.

I'm weighing a crash-to-splash swap at the bar 30 downbeat, but deciding whistle or cuica sounds too gimmicky to include. I'm also debating keeping cowbell versus agogo in the Latin section around bar 25, and whether wood blocks might work better than toms for the breakdown answer at bar 39 — though toms still feel like the nicer choice.

For bar 37, I'm trying to work out a wood block pickup with ghost notes, checking hand assignments and swing timing so the hits land cleanly against the ride pattern without conflicting with the right hand's existing part.

I'm also confirming kick feathering under the ride during the breakdown, checking Latin conga offsets, and verifying hi-hat pedal placement across the groove bars to make sure it stays silent except where fills call for occasional chicks.

For bar 19, I'm working out the drum roll build using a snare crescendo across 32nd notes with alternating hands, adding kick accents at the start of groups, then landing on a crash and kick hit at bar's end while calculating the precise sub-step timing for the final snare hits leading into the transition.

The uneven swung 32nd rhythm actually feels musical rather than mechanical. Now I'm building bar 35's run of 24 32nd notes, alternating high tom pairs across each beat.

Working through the china crash and kick placement at step 12, checking for timing conflicts with the snare so I skip it there to avoid clashing at the tight 50-tick gap. For bars 28-34 I'm keeping the left foot chick simple, hitting only on beats 4 and 12, with bar 35 dropping that entirely except at step 12. For the climax runs at 52-53 I'm alternating right and left hands on the 32nd notes with the right hand landing the crash and kick together, while working out how the right foot's kick pattern fits underneath.

Now I'm laying out the double-bass drumming for bar 54, alternating right and left foot kicks across the sixteenth notes to extend the earlier loop pattern, and setting up a helper function to handle the double-bass hits consistently. For bar 55 I'm going full tutti before cutting to silence, checking that the dynamic envelope drops smoothly from full intensity down to about 0.62 for the release. I'm also filling in the foot patterns for bars 48-51, adding tom fills and kicks at the transition points, then double-checking the double-bass setup at bar 44.

Now I'm designing the hand pattern generator for bar 45, which maps accent positions to crash cymbals or low floor toms alternating by hand while filling remaining steps with tom runs, and making sure the accent keys are handled as integers rather than floats to avoid lookup mismatches. I'm also setting dynamic breakpoints before writing the main sequencing logic, and verifying that no limb gets assigned overlapping hits.

Working through the crash and kick placements across the various bars — bar 4's groove crash, bar 12's development section, bar 28's build with a kick skip at step 0, and bars 30-31 with grouped tom/snare/kick patterns alternating between hi and mid toms. Now I'm moving toward finalizing the full write-up.

I'm defining a level function that interpolates between dynamic breakpoints, returning the appropriate value based on where x falls in the piecewise ranges, with careful near-jump timing so the dynamic level shifts abruptly right before a specific step.

Checking that these levels apply sensibly to the Latin section — ghost notes and slaps at the 0.68 dynamic level still land in reasonable volume ranges after scaling.

Now I'm organizing events by note to compute note-off timings, converting to integer ticks first, then working out duration offsets for each hit including the final hit at 1800. I need to handle cases where two events share the same note and tick — like unison snare hits from different limbs — by keeping only the louder one rather than duplicating.

Building note-off logic...
